audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 1, 2 and 4 disagreed with the already-audited mirror: level 2 was 'Skill', level 3 was 'Yone', and level 6 was given to Ziggs at 7/10 against this page's own whys[4].
audit.why: audits/top/yone__ziggs.json sets the reference as [Ziggs, Yone, Skill, Yone, Yone, Yone, Yone]. Mortal Steel's second cast dashes him forward with a knock-up on a flat 4s, which is exactly why level 2 is his, and Fate Sealed owns level 6.
audit.corrected: Row 1 to Yone (3/10), row 2 to Skill (5/10), row 4 to Yone (4/10) as matched full/content pairs, with whys[1] through whys[6] rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[5] and whys[6] promise the lane 'swings back to you' at first item and that you 'stay ahead' at two, on rows both layers label Yone; phases[4].why still described level 6 as your Mega Inferno Bomb stage.
audit.why: Fate Sealed is 120/100/80s at 1000 range and blinks behind the last champion in a line, pulling everyone toward him — an artillery mage's position is exactly what it deletes. Spirit Cleave is a flat 14s shield that scales with attack speed, so his item timings absorb more of your rotation, not less.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why, whys[5] and whys[6] rewritten with Fate Sealed's cooldown and Spirit Cleave's shield.

audit.whatIsWrong: Soul Unbound is described as a dash he uses 'to dash in and undo the trade', and the page claims the snap-back leaves 'the damage undone'. Neither is what Riot's text says, and no cooldown appears anywhere on the page.
audit.why: Riot kit: Soul Unbound (22/19/16/13/10s) leaves his body behind and grants move speed; when it ends his spirit is forced back to the body and he repeats a portion of the damage he dealt as a spirit. It is not a dash and Riot's text does not say damage he took is undone. His dashes are Mortal Steel's second cast (flat 4s, 450 range) and Fate Sealed.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text, wants.foe[1], dosFull[0].d and dosFull[2].d rewritten with the real behaviour and the 22s.

audit.whatIsWrong: packet.defects: no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere, sequencingCues 0.
audit.why: The punishable cooldown is Soul Unbound — 22s at rank 1 falling to 10s at rank 5, so the safe step-up window shrinks by more than half across the laning phase. That decay is the whole reason the later rows flip to him.
audit.corrected: dosFull[0].d and dosFull[2].d now give both ends of that range as the wait-for-X line.

edits.before: Mega Inferno Bomb online — any chipped target or crashing wave is now your gold. Hold it for the sub-60% HP window.
edits.after: Fate Sealed (120s at rank 1, 1000 range) blinks behind you and pulls — his all-in now beats your poke rotation.

edits.before: Level 2 stays yours — no gap-close yet, so you poke him freely.
edits.after: At 2 Mortal Steel's second cast dashes and knocks you up.

edits.before: Level 3 you zone with mines and out-range his walk-up, keeping trades lopsided.
edits.after: Level 3 you mine his walk-up, but Spirit Cleave (14s) shields the chip.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 remain in your favour as poke forces him to soak damage before six.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 Soul Unbound (22s) lets him commit and then undo the trade.

edits.before: First item swings back to you: item poke and waveclear shove him under tower.
edits.after: At his first crit item Spirit Cleave's shield eats a whole Q rotation.

edits.before: Into 2+ items you stay ahead — out-spaced, he can never open a fight on you.
edits.after: At two items Fate Sealed (80s at rank 3) pulls you clean out of position.

edits.before: His spike. Fate Sealed (R) plus his Soul Unbound (E) return means he can dash in, all-in, and if it fails, E back to safety with the damage undone. Hold Satchel Charge to blast yourself out of his Q3 knock-up, and don't blow it early — his E snap-back baits panic buttons.
edits.after: His spike. Fate Sealed (120s) blinks behind the last champion in a line and drags everyone toward him, and Soul Unbound (22s at rank 1) lets him commit in spirit form and snap back to his body after. Hold Satchel for the Q3 knock-up and don't spend it early — the snap-back baits panic buttons.

edits.before: Use Soul Unbound (E) to dash in and undo the trade if it fails
edits.after: Use Soul Unbound to commit, then snap back to his body

edits.before: His burst window — survive it and punish the body he snaps back to. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: Soul Unbound is 22s at rank 1 and 10s at rank 5 — step up in that gap and punish the body he snaps back to.

edits.before: Yone whiffs Soul Unbound and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: Yone whiffs Soul Unbound — that is a 22s window at rank 1.

notes: Three of the four packet suspectNames are FALSE POSITIVES: 'Hold Satchel Charge' and 'Save Satchel Charge' are Ziggs' own W, and 'His Soul Unbound' is Yone's real E. The genuine error the flag was pointing near is that Soul Unbound was called a dash — fixed. Did not assert that the snap-back undoes damage he took; Riot's text says only that he repeats a portion of the damage he dealt. Satchel's percentHealth derived flag contradicts Riot's W description and was not written to the page, matching the mirror.
